title: Spoken English — Everyday Practice
subtitle: Listen, repeat and role-play real conversations between your classes
description: A supporting practice course for Al Mihad Spoken English students. Each unit has short conversations you can listen to line by line, slow down and role-play, useful phrases, and one small speaking task that your trainer listens to and gives feedback on. Your main learning happens in class — use this course to practise for 10–15 minutes a day.
howTo: Open a conversation and press Listen. Tap any line to hear it again, or slow it down.
Press Role-play, choose a person, and say their lines when it is your turn.
Read the Useful phrases and say each one aloud.
At the end of each unit, record the speaking task (about 1 minute). Your trainer will reply with tips.

units.title: Unit 1 — Introducing yourself
units.summary: Say hello, introduce yourself, and talk about your home, family and job.

items.title: Meeting someone new
items.body: Two new students meet before class. Notice how they give their name, where they are from and where they live.

lines.speaker: Priya
lines.text: Hi! I don't think we've met. I'm Priya.

lines.speaker: Ahmed
lines.text: Hello, Priya. I'm Ahmed. Nice to meet you.

lines.speaker: Priya
lines.text: Nice to meet you too. Where are you from, Ahmed?

lines.speaker: Ahmed
lines.text: I'm from Egypt, but I live in Sharjah now. And you?

lines.speaker: Priya
lines.text: I'm from Kerala, in India. I live in Al Nahda, near the park.

lines.speaker: Ahmed
lines.text: Oh, that's close to here. How long have you been in the UAE?

lines.speaker: Priya
lines.text: About two years. I came here for work.

lines.speaker: Ahmed
lines.text: Me too. Well, I'm happy we are in the same class.

items.title: How are you? — different ways to ask and answer
items.body: There are many ways to greet people. Some are formal (for work), some are friendly (for friends).

lines.speaker: Sara
lines.text: Good morning, Mr. Joseph. How are you today?

lines.speaker: Joseph
lines.text: Good morning, Sara. I'm very well, thank you. And you?

lines.speaker: Sara
lines.text: I'm fine, thank you.

lines.speaker: Joseph
lines.text: Hey Sara! How's it going?

lines.speaker: Sara
lines.text: Not bad! A little busy, but good. What about you?

lines.speaker: Joseph
lines.text: Same here. How was your weekend?

lines.speaker: Sara
lines.text: It was great. I visited my cousin in Dubai.

lines.speaker: Joseph
lines.text: Sounds nice. Have a good day!

lines.speaker: Sara
lines.text: You too. See you later!

items.title: Useful phrases — introductions and greetings
items.body:
## Introducing yourself
- My name is … / I'm …
- I'm from … (country / state / city)
- I live in … (area / city)
- I work as a … / I work at …
- I'm learning English because …

## Asking about others
- Where are you from?
- Where do you live?
- What do you do? (= What is your job?)
- How long have you been in the UAE?

## How are you? — answers
| Formal | Friendly |
|---|---|
| I'm very well, thank you. | Not bad! |
| I'm fine, thank you. And you? | Pretty good, thanks. |
| Very well, thank you for asking. | Same as always! |

## Common mistakes
- ✗ I am working in a hospital since 2 years. → ✓ I have worked in a hospital for two years.
- ✗ My name is Priya and I am belongs to Kerala. → ✓ My name is Priya and I am from Kerala.
- ✗ What is your good name? → ✓ What is your name?

items.title: Talking about home and family
items.body: Two colleagues talk about where they live and who they live with.

lines.speaker: Fatima
lines.text: Ravi, do you live with your family here?

lines.speaker: Ravi
lines.text: Yes, I live with my wife and my two children.

lines.speaker: Fatima
lines.text: That's nice. How old are your children?

lines.speaker: Ravi
lines.text: My son is eight and my daughter is five. They go to school in Sharjah.

lines.speaker: Fatima
lines.text: Do you live in a flat or a villa?

lines.speaker: Ravi
lines.text: We live in a two-bedroom flat. It's small, but it's comfortable. What about you?

lines.speaker: Fatima
lines.text: I share a flat with two friends. My parents and my brother live back home in Pakistan.

lines.speaker: Ravi
lines.text: You must miss them.

lines.speaker: Fatima
lines.text: I do. We video call every evening.

items.title: Your job and what you do
items.body: Listen to how people describe their job and their daily work.

lines.speaker: Ahmed
lines.text: So, Priya, what do you do?

lines.speaker: Priya
lines.text: I'm a staff nurse. I work at a clinic in Al Qasimia.

lines.speaker: Ahmed
lines.text: That sounds like hard work. What are your working hours?

lines.speaker: Priya
lines.text: I work from eight in the morning to five in the evening, six days a week.

lines.speaker: Ahmed
lines.text: What do you do every day?

lines.speaker: Priya
lines.text: I check patients, give medicines and help the doctors. And you, what is your job?

lines.speaker: Ahmed
lines.text: I'm a sales executive in an electronics shop. I talk to customers and explain the products.

lines.speaker: Priya
lines.text: So you need good English for your job too.

lines.speaker: Ahmed
lines.text: Exactly. That's why I joined this course.

items.title: Speaking task — Introduce yourself
items.prompt:
Record a short introduction (about 1 minute). Say at least 6 sentences:
• your name
• where you are from
• where you live now and who you live with
• your job and your working hours
• one thing you like to do in your free time
• why you are learning English
items.tips: Speak slowly and clearly. It is fine to make mistakes — your trainer will help you.

units.title: Unit 2 — Everyday situations
units.summary: Shopping, at the park, and asking for and giving directions.

items.title: At the supermarket
items.body: A customer asks a shop assistant for help and pays at the counter.

lines.speaker: Customer
lines.text: Excuse me, where can I find the rice?

lines.speaker: Assistant
lines.text: It's in aisle five, next to the flour and the oil.

lines.speaker: Customer
lines.text: Thank you. Do you have this in a bigger pack?

lines.speaker: Assistant
lines.text: Yes, we have a ten-kilo bag. It's on the bottom shelf.

lines.speaker: Customer
lines.text: Great. Is there any offer on it this week?

lines.speaker: Assistant
lines.text: Yes, it's fifteen percent off until Friday.

lines.speaker: Customer
lines.text: Perfect. Can I pay by card at the counter?

lines.speaker: Assistant
lines.text: Of course. Would you like a bag?

lines.speaker: Customer
lines.text: No, thank you. I brought my own.

items.title: At the park
items.body: Two neighbours start a friendly conversation in the evening at the park.

lines.speaker: Joseph
lines.text: Good evening! Do you come here every day?

lines.speaker: Sara
lines.text: Almost every day. I walk for thirty minutes after work.

lines.speaker: Joseph
lines.text: That's a good habit. The weather is lovely this time of year.

lines.speaker: Sara
lines.text: Yes, it's not too hot in the evening now. Is that your son?

lines.speaker: Joseph
lines.text: Yes, that's Daniel, on the swings. He loves coming here.

lines.speaker: Sara
lines.text: He looks very happy. Is the play area open on Fridays too?

lines.speaker: Joseph
lines.text: Yes, but it gets very crowded. Saturday morning is quieter.

lines.speaker: Sara
lines.text: Thanks for the tip. Enjoy your evening!

items.title: Asking for and giving directions
items.body: Someone is looking for a pharmacy. Listen for the direction words: straight, turn left, opposite, next to.

lines.speaker: Ravi
lines.text: Excuse me, is there a pharmacy near here?

lines.speaker: Fatima
lines.text: Yes, there's one on the main road. It's about five minutes on foot.

lines.speaker: Ravi
lines.text: How do I get there?

lines.speaker: Fatima
lines.text: Go straight along this street until you reach the traffic signal.

lines.speaker: Fatima
lines.text: Then turn left. The pharmacy is on your right, opposite the bank, next to a small café.

lines.speaker: Ravi
lines.text: So, straight to the signal, turn left, and it's opposite the bank?

lines.speaker: Fatima
lines.text: That's right. You can't miss it.

lines.speaker: Ravi
lines.text: Thank you so much for your help.

lines.speaker: Fatima
lines.text: You're welcome.

items.title: Useful phrases — shopping and directions
items.body:
## In a shop
- Excuse me, where can I find …?
- Do you have this in a bigger / smaller size?
- How much is this? / Is there any offer?
- Can I pay by card / in cash?
- Can I return this if it doesn't fit?

## Asking for directions
- Excuse me, is there a … near here?
- How do I get to …?
- Is it far from here? / Can I walk there?

## Giving directions
| Words | Example |
|---|---|
| go straight | Go straight for 200 metres. |
| turn left / right | Turn right at the traffic signal. |
| opposite | It's opposite the bank. |
| next to / beside | It's next to the café. |
| between | It's between the mosque and the school. |
| at the corner | The shop is at the corner. |

## Common mistakes
- ✗ Where is the near pharmacy? → ✓ Where is the nearest pharmacy?
- ✗ Take left. → ✓ Turn left.
- ✗ How much this is? → ✓ How much is this?

items.title: Speaking task — Give directions
items.prompt: A new neighbour asks you how to get from your building to the nearest supermarket (or bus stop). Record clear directions (about 1 minute). Use at least four of: go straight, turn left, turn right, opposite, next to, between, at the corner.
items.tips: Imagine you are walking the route. Say each step in order.

units.title: Unit 3 — Speaking in paragraphs
units.summary: Talk for at least five sentences about a picture or a real situation.

items.title: How to speak in a paragraph (5 sentences)
items.body:
When you describe a picture or a situation, answer these five questions — one sentence each:

1. **Where** is it? — *This is a busy supermarket in the evening.*
2. **Who** is there? — *I can see many families and some shop staff.*
3. **What** are they doing? — *People are pushing trolleys and choosing fruit.*
4. **What else** do you notice? — *There is a long queue at the counter.*
5. **How** does it feel / what do you think? — *It looks busy, but everyone seems happy.*

## Linking words
first, then, next, also, but, because, so, finally

## Tips
- Use *there is / there are* to describe.
- Use *-ing* for actions happening now: *A man **is** carry**ing** a box.*
- Finish with your opinion or feeling.

items.title: Model answer — A busy market
items.body: Listen to a model paragraph. Then pause and say your own version.

lines.speaker: Model
lines.text: This is a busy fish and vegetable market early in the morning.

lines.speaker: Model
lines.text: There are many shops in a long row, and there are lots of people everywhere.

lines.speaker: Model
lines.text: Some shopkeepers are shouting their prices, and customers are choosing fresh vegetables.

lines.speaker: Model
lines.text: I can also see a delivery man carrying big boxes of tomatoes to a truck.

lines.speaker: Model
lines.text: It is noisy and crowded, but I like the energy of a morning market.

items.title: Model answer — My last weekend
items.body: A model paragraph about a real situation, using past tense.

lines.speaker: Model
lines.text: Last Friday, I spent the day with my family at Al Majaz Waterfront.

lines.speaker: Model
lines.text: We reached there in the afternoon, when the weather was cool.

lines.speaker: Model
lines.text: First, the children played in the park, and then we walked along the water.

lines.speaker: Model
lines.text: In the evening, we watched the musical fountain and had dinner at a small restaurant.

lines.speaker: Model
lines.text: It was a simple day, but we were very happy and relaxed.

items.title: Speaking task — Describe a situation
items.prompt:
Choose ONE situation and speak for about 1 minute — at least 5 sentences:
• A bus stop in the morning
• Your favourite restaurant at lunchtime
• Your workplace on a busy day

Use the five questions: Where? Who? What are they doing? What else? How does it feel?
items.tips: Use linking words: first, then, also, but, because, finally.

units.title: Unit 4 — Business communication
units.summary: Speak politely and professionally: phone calls, requests to your manager, and meeting clients.

items.title: Answering a phone call at work
items.body: A receptionist answers a call from a client. Notice the polite phrases.

lines.speaker: Receptionist
lines.text: Good morning, Gulf Star Trading. This is Anitha speaking. How may I help you?

lines.speaker: Client
lines.text: Good morning. Could I speak to Mr. Hassan in the accounts department, please?

lines.speaker: Receptionist
lines.text: May I know who is calling, please?

lines.speaker: Client
lines.text: This is Daniel Mathew from Blue Line Logistics.

lines.speaker: Receptionist
lines.text: Thank you, Mr. Mathew. I'm sorry, Mr. Hassan is in a meeting right now. Would you like to leave a message?

lines.speaker: Client
lines.text: Yes, please. Could you ask him to call me back about invoice number four-five-two?

lines.speaker: Receptionist
lines.text: Certainly. May I have your phone number?

lines.speaker: Client
lines.text: It's oh-five-oh, one-two-three, four-five-six-seven.

lines.speaker: Receptionist
lines.text: Thank you. I'll pass on your message as soon as he is free.

lines.speaker: Client
lines.text: Thank you for your help. Goodbye.

items.title: Asking your manager for leave
items.body: An employee asks for two days of leave. Notice: Could I…? / Would it be possible…?

lines.speaker: Employee
lines.text: Excuse me, Ms. Reena. Do you have a minute?

lines.speaker: Manager
lines.text: Sure, Ravi. What is it?

lines.speaker: Employee
lines.text: Would it be possible to take leave next Monday and Tuesday? My sister is getting married.

lines.speaker: Manager
lines.text: Congratulations! Let me check the schedule. Who will cover your work?

lines.speaker: Employee
lines.text: I have spoken to Arun. He has agreed to handle my customers on those days.

lines.speaker: Manager
lines.text: That's good planning. Please send me a leave request by email today.

lines.speaker: Employee
lines.text: Of course. I'll send it right away. Thank you for understanding.

lines.speaker: Manager
lines.text: No problem. Enjoy the wedding.

items.title: Meeting a client for the first time
items.body: A sales executive meets a new client at the office.

lines.speaker: Ahmed
lines.text: Good afternoon, Ms. Lina. Welcome to our office. I'm Ahmed, the sales executive.

lines.speaker: Lina
lines.text: Good afternoon, Ahmed. Thank you for meeting me.

lines.speaker: Ahmed
lines.text: It's a pleasure. Please have a seat. Would you like some tea or coffee?

lines.speaker: Lina
lines.text: Just water, please. Thank you.

lines.speaker: Ahmed
lines.text: Before we start, could you tell me a little about your company's needs?

lines.speaker: Lina
lines.text: Of course. We need twenty laptops for our new staff before the end of the month.

lines.speaker: Ahmed
lines.text: That's no problem. I'll show you three options, and then I can send you a quotation by email today.

lines.speaker: Lina
lines.text: That sounds perfect.

items.title: Useful phrases — speaking professionally
items.body:
## Polite requests
| Too direct | Professional |
|---|---|
| Give me the report. | Could you send me the report, please? |
| I want leave on Monday. | Would it be possible to take leave on Monday? |
| Call me back. | Could you call me back when you are free? |
| What? | Sorry, could you repeat that, please? |

## On the phone
- Good morning, [company]. This is … speaking. How may I help you?
- May I know who is calling, please?
- I'm sorry, he is not available right now. Would you like to leave a message?
- I'll pass on your message.

## In meetings
- Thank you for your time.
- Could you tell me a little about …?
- Let me check and get back to you.
- I'll send you the details by email today.

## Common mistakes
- ✗ Kindly do the needful. → ✓ Could you please take care of this?
- ✗ I will revert back. → ✓ I will get back to you.
- ✗ Please do one thing, call him. → ✓ Could you please call him?

items.title: Speaking task — Leave a voicemail for a client
items.prompt:
You need to move tomorrow's 10 a.m. meeting with a client to Thursday. Leave a short, polite voicemail (about 1 minute):
• greet the client and say who you are and your company
• explain the change and give a short reason
• suggest a new time
• ask them to confirm, and give your phone number
• thank them and say goodbye
items.tips: Use: I'm calling to…, Would it be possible…?, Could you please confirm…?
